premise: A college dropout who initially traded in ball-bearings builds a massive Indian supermarket retail empire from scratch.
hook: He started his career as a modest stock market speculator before building the country's most profitable retail chain.
key_facts: Dropped out of Mumbai University commerce studies after his father's death.
Initially traded in the stock market before launching the Avenue Supermarts retail chain.
Founded the D-Mart supermarket brand in 2002.
Became one of India's wealthiest self-made entrepreneurs.

premise: An orphaned daughter of emancipated slaves who built a haircare empire to become one of the first self-made female millionaires in America.
hook: Born into poverty just years after the end of American slavery, she turned a scalp ailment into a multi-million-dollar enterprise.
key_facts: Born Sarah Breedlove on a cotton plantation in Louisiana in 1867.
Suffered severe hair loss due to poor scalp health and harsh chemical products of the era.
Developed and marketed a specialized line of hair products and treatments for African American hair.
Employed thousands of women as sales agents, providing financial independence.

premise: A young American hitchhiker who traveled across Europe and the Middle East on foot to find spiritual truth in India.
hook: He left home with almost no money, traveling across continents with just a sleeping bag and a backpack.
key_facts: Grew up in Chicago in a middle-class family.
Hitchhiked across Europe and the Middle East during the early 1970s.
Crossed the border into India with minimal resources.
Became a prominent spiritual leader and author based in Mumbai.

premise: How an engineer pooled a small amount of capital borrowed from his wife to build a global IT giant from a small bedroom.
hook: One of India's most successful technology pioneers started his company with just a few hundred dollars and a vision for software outsourcing.
key_facts: Co-founded Infosys in Pune, India, in 1981 with six other software professionals.
Started operations with minimal capital, initially borrowing seed money from his wife Sudha Murthy.
Helped pioneer the global software services industry model in India.
Served as CEO and later Chairman of the Board, transforming the firm into a multinational corporation.

premise: The famous disappearance of the detective novelist in 1926 that triggered a massive 11-day national manhunt.
hook: The world's bestselling mystery writer pulled off a real-life disappearance that baffled police and captivated the British press.
key_facts: Her abandoned car was found perched above a chalk quarry in Surrey in December 1926
Sparked a 10-day police search involving over 1,000 officers and hundreds of civilian volunteers
Found staying at the Swan Hydropathic Hotel in Harrogate under an assumed name linked to her husband's mistress
Never publicly explained the exact reasons behind her sudden disappearance

premise: How a young boy from Tamil Nadu learned chess in the Philippines and became India's first grandmaster.
hook: Before he became a five-time World Chess Champion, he learned the rules of the game from his mother in a quiet coastal suburb.
key_facts: Born in Mayiladuthurai, Tamil Nadu, and raised partly in Chennai and the Philippines
Taught the rules of chess by his mother, Susheela, at age six
Became India's first International Grandmaster in 1988 at the age of 18
Won the World Chess Championship five times across different formats

premise: The self-taught mathematical genius from Erode who mailed pages of complex formulas to a Cambridge professor out of the blue.
hook: A low-level shipping clerk with no formal university degree mailed raw mathematical theorems to England that changed modern math forever.
key_facts: Grew up in Erode and Kumbakonam, Tamil Nadu, failing college exams because he neglected non-math subjects
Worked as a routine shipping clerk in Madras to support his family while doing mathematics on slates
Sent unrequested letters containing advanced theorems to British mathematician G.H. Hardy in 1913
Traveled to Trinity College, Cambridge, where he was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society
